tips.comment: Good trainer Ralph Beckett has been patient with the 3yo filly. Just one career run, last Sept, a winning start when well supported in the market. She’s had 8 months off the track to get stronger. A good sign that he’s happy to pitch in a Listed contest on her return. Unexposed and this is a very weak looking contest.

Nice win LTO at Ascot 1L from Brave Mission. Made all that day over CD where it's very difficult to make the running and win. No such bias here at Goodwood where its 7f only slightly favors hold-up horses. Not a lot of pace on here with running likely to be made by this one with Bob Mali up close. Should be able to dictate the fractions. Obviously rising in the weights quite rapidly, but in a race run to suit, may be able to hold on and should at least place.

Just five career runs for the 3yo filly, form 32132. She was only beaten a neck in a 20-runner £193K sales race last September. Receiving some weight that day, but she was beaten by two runners rated 100 and 114. Still unexposed, and an 8-month break can see some improvement. A handicap mark of 87 can give her a chance.

This price looks like an oversight. The Portman runner won on seasonal bow with any amount in hand, and that was a career-best run. He looked before the race that the run would bring him on but won in such a manner it's difficult not to see him following up with race conditions in his favor in terms of ground and weight. Plus, he has the beating of several of these on that Palace House at Newmarket.

Will preface with I don't usually like handicappers stepping into Graded races. However, he's won for me the last twice and is quite a likeable horse. 5f bias here favors held-up horses and those drawn high, ticks both boxes. Has looked a Group horse in the making both races this season and looked very smart when closing from all the way back at York last time out. Possibly flattered by the pace collapse that day, but nonetheless, doing it under the weight in that style is impressive. Not yet convinced on Rumstar's Newmarket form with a few clearly needing the run, and one would imagine Mgheera prefers a bit softer having done all her racing in France. Presume Starlust to come on for the run and looks one to watch for now.

Impressed with his finishing speed last time as he stayed on strongly up the Newmarket hill to win going away. Form has worked out alright with both the 2nd and 4th running well since off similar marks. Has gone up 6lb but his record in 1m handicaps on turf read as 52312111. Winner of his last three and no reason to think he has stopped now.
Candonomore still runs off a reasonable handicap of 80, and Amie Waugh claims 3lb. Tim Easterby is in decent form, but winners are scarce, so EW seems the way to go with 4 places available.

Dashing Darcey is having just his 2nd run for trainer Geoff Harker. His 1st run was in the Cl2 Lincoln at Doncaster where he was hampered and denied a clear run . Dropping back into Cl3 company will suit. He has won on good ground and raced okay at Ascot on good to firm ground. SDS has been booked to do the steering with 2 rides and 1 win. Should be in the mix at a decent price.

The 5yo is a standout on the ratings in this Listed contest. She was a smart 2L winner of a 14 runner Group 2 contest at Royal Ascot last summer on fast ground. She’ll be better for the Group 2 return run three weeks ago.

Quite an impressive performance dropped back to 6f last time out. 1.75L clear from Ides Of March, who had been backed as though defeat was out of the question. But even ignoring the fact Ryan had to take him wide, I think it would still have been a close race between the two. Realistically, it was a Group level performance, and with being a gelding and unable to run in the Commonwealth, this seems the logical next step. Big Mojo probably rates as the biggest danger. However, King Charles Stakes appears to be the target, so is 6f really what he wants? No doubt he gets it, but he's not a horse I've ever really sided with and would need to do something impressive to get me onside. Powerful Glory is also interesting but lacks experience here as well as race fitness and would be hard to back.

The 3yo ran some big races on fast ground last year, Group 2 and Group 1 level, finishing the year off with a narrow defeat at the Breeders' Cup. Two good wins this year - high RPR ratings - and come here fresh after a 6-week break. He beat main rival 'Big Mojo' in that Breeders' Cup race last November and can confirm that form in this Group 2 contest. 'Symbol' is turned out quickly after winning last week.

Unbeaten colt who showed excellent acceleration to win the Group 2 Mill Reef Stakes on just his second start. Big potential on return and could be anything ??' slight concern is the 245-day layoff, but respected as a major threat if fit.

I think 5/1 is a very fair price for a horse I believe could be listed class and certainly has a big handicap in him. He may well get his form franked again if Transparent was to run and win at Goodwood on Friday also, though the form has already received a boost after the win of the third next time by over 4 lengths. A course winner as a 2-year-old last year, he has gone up 8 lb but I don't think it will stop a horse who showed a good turn of foot to win.

Unbeaten in two runs over this distance and on similar ground, Teroomm makes his handicap debut after a strong novice win at Thirsk. He’s clearly progressive and represents a powerful yard, suggesting he’s capable of further improvement. While this is a rise in class, his perfect record and unexposed profile make him the one to beat.

Three starts for the well-bred 3yo colt, form 221. Interesting that the trainer has started him on the AW and is now making his turf debut, with a £51K first prize for this handicap. The form of his close 2nd of 14 on his second start is looking strong now. Only doing what was needed to win a novice stakes five weeks ago. His opening mark of 85 is attractive.

Paul Mulrennan does not ride many for Ed Walker but was 3rd on Fort George at Newcastle. The 3-year-old won last time out and is up 5lb, which looks fair and should give a good account of himself over the same trip. EW 4 places.

The 2yo filly was a smart 4L winner of a 12-runner maiden race at the start of the month. 5f on fast ground. A shade unlucky just over a week ago in a decent-looking Listed contest, beaten 2L, but she had an awkward start and was a little lit up. Worth another chance in this conditions race with the trip and conditions suiting her.

The 2yo colt was a close 3rd on his debut two weeks ago, losing out in the last 100 yards. The race was won by a race fit and useful looking Charlie Appleby trained runner. The selection should improve for the run and he might not meet one of that calibre in this conditions race.

Ryan Moore is booked for his only ride of the day. He was successful on the selection in a maiden 2 starts ago. He then ran with credit in his final 2-year-old start 223 days ago at Newmarket, and the AOB yard have won 7 of the last 12 renewals.
Deserves this step up in class, tackling Group company for the first time, after destroying a field of maidens by 5L LTO. Will have the fitness edge over some of these, so is worth a bet.
3rd in the Ballysax, sandwiched in-between black type winning horses. Time for this Night of Thunder colt to win a black type. Dropping back to his winning maiden trip may just do the trick.

Shackleton has the best form but all of his rivals have the benefit of a recent run. His stablemate Thrice ran as if needing his seasonal debut at Chester but has some decent form in the book and should strip fitter today.

Keke is a 5-year-old gelding trained by sprint specialist Edward Lynam. He is a talented horse with 5 wins out of 13 starts. He is a two-time course winner, once over CD, and is ground versatile. He posted a career-high RPR of 101 and runs off 92 today, so he is feasibly well treated. He finished 4th out of 25 in the Bold Lad Sprint over CD just three starts back, beaten just 1.75 lengths. He handles big fields and seems to thrive at the Curragh. He is my short-priced banker of the day under W J Lee.

I’m willing to take a tentative poke here with Johnny Murtagh’s 5yr old gelding DAAMBERDIPLOMAT, who drops significantly in class after contesting a competitive Class 2 all-weather sprint (6f) at Newcastle 35 days ago (beaten 4¾ lengths).
This son of COTAI GLORY has just one turf win to his name but hasn’t run badly at the Curragh - most notably finishing 4th on his last visit, just a head behind today’s rival COLLECTIVE POWER. Jockey Ben Coen returns to the saddle, having partnered DAAMBERDIPLOMAT to 2 of his 4 career wins. Coen is in solid form, with a 31.82% place strike rate over the past month and 23.92% here at the Curragh across five years. Even more encouraging is his 40.45% place strike rate for Murtagh in the past year - part of 8 recent wins for the yard in the past 30 days.
So, why tentative? It’s no secret this charge prefers the all-weather, and the possible forecasted rain could compromise his chances - though one would assume the trainer would withdraw him if the ground goes against him.
Still, at 20/1, 5 places and a big class drop, I’m happy to have a little skin in the game.

Collective Power is worth a play at odds of 12-1. Low in this handicap running off a mark of 82 and Sorcha Woods claims an apprentice's 7lbs allowance. Ted Lynam brings a strong string to the Curragh this afternoon. Second and then first for this jockey on final two AW starts at Dundalk before running decently at Naas last time out. Struggled with traffic problems there, doing his best work late on. Seven years of age with a career tally of 8 wins from 64 runs.

LITTLE QUEENIE is treated well by being eased a further 4lb in the handicap. That is on the back of her reappoearance effort and she should strip fitter for that effort. With potential now to be seen to good effect second run back she appeals as a value each-way play.

Decent effort at Cork last time, his first start for 9 months, when a close up 5th over 7f. Travelled well during the race but failed to get a clear run at a critical stage so did well to finish as close as he did. Decent place claims.

Five career wins include three over today's course and distance. Found things happening too fast dropped to five furlongs for his seasonal return, but will have come on for that first outing in well over five months. He has to be in the mix racing over a track and trip that clearly suits.

TANGO FLARE gets an experienced jockey booked looking favourably treated for his reappearance. He has shown winning form when returning for a new season and he comes from a yard who now how to get one ready for a punt in handicap company under both codes.
Low draw, tough mark remark the Racing Post, but with form figures of 3, 2, 2, 1, 5, albeit on the all-weather, we shouldn't be quite written off just yet.

Ontheropes takes a drop in class for this long-distance hunter's chase. He has a very good past record, which included 5th in last year's Scottish Grand National. Although his only point win was this January, his only chase win was back in October 2021.

GRANGE SOLIDIER could be worth chancing sent out under rules at a similar time last year which resulted in a win. He showed signs when pointing latest that he may be about to come back to hand , so potentially a spring developer he appeals.

Looks a good thing here. Stable in red-hot form. 50% strike rate in May, 10 winners from 20 runners. Selection was not knocked about on debut last time, having been caught further back than ideal and will come on for the run and improve.

Glory To Be makes its debut at 3yo instead of 2yo and I can see why. Yard will quickly move on from this to bigger things. When looking into it's pedigree the 2yo form isn't good. When looking at parents 3yo form the difference is incredible c2 c1 group races plenty of prize money. This is the angle this shrewd yard will be aiming at after this. 20/1 e/w nap.

Team Twomey are in sparkling form, and their entry is predictably a short-priced favourite. But debutant Charasson could well make a race of it. The Kodiac filly is extremely well-related and with a yard who are also in fine form.

Thrice raced daughter of No Nay Never & Lucky At The Bay ( Dam's sire Lucky Pulpit ) who makes her seasonal reappearance run here after a 203 day break likely to be much better built and more professional over on the business end now as a 3yo D Dias's inmate is likely to progress well this term and is open to plenty of improvement especially now as a 3yo steps up in trip tackling the full 6 furlong trip for the first time that most certainly being a good move by her connections as this new trip can help bring out that improvement jockey G M Ryan takes the ride and can give Never Not Lucky the perfect ride here at the Curragh expect this good looking chestnut to be a whole different proposition
Noble Name fought back well at Tipperary when 3rd in a mares' bumper following her win in a point, and there is a good chance that she can outbattle Better Times and Cinnamon Roll in this bumper.
Clearly struggling to get 3 miles in PTP races, but he's not badly bred and with a top yard, so can perhaps be seen to better effect now trying a bumper.

Looked potentially smart when winning his bumper just over a year ago. Plenty of decent horses have come out of that race subsequently. Has since had 2 runs over hurdles, including on reappearance last time when runner-up. Will appreciate the step up in trip today and is the one to beat.

Hills Of Glory was just pipped at the post at Naas in December over this distance in what was to date the closest call in search of the maiden win. It is that showing which provides the basis for siding with here at a similar price.
Jazz De Cotte has some decent form but is giving weight away to all but one rival. Perhaps his stablemate, Welcome Back, can get his jumping together and begin to realize his undoubted potential.

ECO PETE won a bumper race at this course in December 2021. His last two races have been over fences, but prior to that, he ran here over 22f. That race was last August where he finished 6th of 7 behind Intense Approach. Dropped in trip today, he may be able to gain a first hurdle win on his 11th attempt. He has previously finished placed three times. His official rating of 102 gives him a chance of getting involved.

The model I run suggests ParkGarve can win this race. ParkGarve lines up here with a relatively high RPR, but goes out carrying a relatively low weight when comparing to the other 15 runners in this race. ParkGarve is the only horse here who has placed or run any kind of form recently, coming third 10 days ago. The model has indicated a 'very low' stake reading, which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4. This is largely as a result of the small gap in predicted positioning to second place.

Ocean Manifest is a 4-year-old making a stable debut for Stephen Thorne, a trainer in great form, winning with his last three runners. If reproducing his debut run at Fairyhouse last year, when he finished 3/16 behind Four Blondes under Seammie Heffernan, posting aa RPR of 83, the 3/16 Monasterboice won the next three races. The 4/16 Leaders Listen won on the next start, and the 5/16 Artful Approach also won on the next start. He has an absence to overcome, but with the yard in such good form, Ocean Manifest has to be considered off a lowly mark of 71 with Jack Kearney's 3lb apprentice claim.
Won over a mile last time out. Interesting to see Colin Keane hang around to assist as Port Louis attempts to defy a 4lb hike and may well be able to do so back at his optimum trip.

A Friday night barnburner at the Curragh - what’s not to like? A wide-open 23-runner mile handicap, and while we’re not quite in “close your eyes and throw a dart” territory, it’s still fiercely competitive. That said, I’m sticking with Chris Timmons’ 4-year-old filly AUBURN AVENUE, who I tipped here 18 days ago (7f, Good).
She didn’t get the smoothest of passages that day - checked a couple of times - but stayed on well to finish fifth, showing a willing attitude. This daughter of PHOENIX OF SPAIN has been dropped 3lbs for that effort and now gets a significant jockey upgrade. Chris Hayes takes over in the saddle and arrives here in fine form, with a 35.29% place strike rate over the past month and a strong 25.41% place rate at the Curragh over the past five years.
There is a slight concern if the forecast early evening showers affect the going, but she didn’t disgrace herself on heavy going at Leopardstown (9f) last October. Now stepping up in trip, racing off a 13lb lower mark than her last Curragh outing in stronger company, and with a top rider booked, I’ll stay loyal and give this girl another chance.

Now 4 pounds lower today. Showhound had been in solid form earlier in the year, including a win at Newcastle in January, and wasn’t disgraced when mid-division in a massive 25 runner handicap here last time, where he was only 7 lengths off the winner despite being below his best. The return of cheekpieces could sharpen him up, and he's got a more manageable race this time. Definite player if back to his earlier form.

This went in my tracker some years ago, and I might have mentioned it before in my write-ups that I thought Cordouan had some talent but seemed to get distracted and that some form of headgear would help. Well, it did finally happen last August, and it won. It has now changed hands, and the headgear has gone (I believe). I didn't bet on either race this year but did get place money (Skybet) in the first race, which I thought was a stretch first up over 1m 2f and was a decent 5th last time out back down to today's trip of 1m. It had a slow start, so filled in at the rear and then had some traffic problems, so pretty good really. 2lb down, and the headgear looks a thing of the past.

Shigar looks interesting at a big price in the concluding handicap. He has won 3 times on the flat, with two coming in Britain. He was placed 4 times last season before winning a Navan handicap off a mark of 80. He has been unplaced in two races off 84 since, the last being on seasonal debut at Cork earlier this month. He has, though, been dropped to 81, and Jamie Orr claims 10 lbs. He looks a good each-way bet with 6 places on offer.

BUCKLES AND BOLTS could fare much better with the headgear removed down in trip today. He is one of multiple entries for a shrewd Irish yard in Sheila Lavery and with an in-form claming apprentice jockey aboard this potential improver from his reduced mark could surprise.

Not an obvious choice but wasn't beaten far on handicap debut at Leopardstown last month, and subsequently had no luck in running over seven furlongs here earlier this month. Came up against some much higher rated opponents at Killarney latest, and certainly far from disgraced on his first attempt at a mile. Can go well returning to handicap company.

MIRACLE BEAUTY has the benefit of being drawn high here. She won her maiden at Naas in October and was a beaten favourite last time out when having her first run in a handicap at Naas over 6f. She wears first time cheekpieces here. Sure to go well.

Staysound Susie won twice last season and is now back down to that last winning mark. She was beaten just 0.5 lengths at Naas 11 days ago and down 2 lbs. Looks like a good EW bet with 4 places on offer.

Completely destroyed her field on penultimate start at Dundalk. Not quite in the same form last time under 8 lb extra, and the handicapper has given her a couple of pounds respite, so she must have a chance.
The experienced Greek Flower is a consistent sort who often goes well fresh and she might be able to defy top weight here with Jamie Powell taking off 3lb.

Island Girl makes plenty of appeal at a double figure price in an open looking race at the Curragh today. The filly ran a promising third last time out and looks primed to win soon with luck in running.

She’s entered off a mark of 81 in what looks a wide-open contest, and with good to firm ground forecast, conditions should be ideal. Adrian Murray has placed her well here, and this step back up in trip combined with the big-field scenario should allow her to settle early and finish late, which looks to be her preferred running style.
While she’ll need to step forward from what she’s shown so far, I think there’s more to come, and she looks overpriced at current odds. She’s one of those lightly raced types that could pop up in a race like this, especially with a strong pace to aim at.

A winner at 6f on yielding ground, well beaten behind East Hampton on reappearance at Naas over 7f soft to yielding in March. Has had 2 months off, probably waiting for better going as the yard is in excellent form. Trying cheekpieces for the first time, should be in the mix. NAP.

ROSATO is an interesting filly arriving fresh at the foot of the weights for a shrewd yard. From her still modest mark she woud of course be eligible for weaker handicaps than she faces here , but now a four year old she may have developed well in her time spent on the sidelines and she has an often favoured high draw over this straight six furlongs.

Sights Unseen keeps knocking on the door but finding one too good, and I wouldn't fancy him if it comes to a battle with the experienced campaigner True Destiny, who ran his usual wholehearted race last time out and can register a 9th career success tonight.

SIR CARNEGIE ran well on his penultimate start suggesting he had a race of this nature in him. He has a sound sire for races in Ireland under the NH code and he remains a five year old capable of progress from his lowly hurdles mark.

We are coming from maiden hurdles, point-to-points, and non-handicap chases here, into a handicap hurdle. It's difficult to weigh up our chances in many ways, but it could equally be good as it could be bad. 3rd LTO in a point.

Ran to a fairly useful level in a light two year old campaign, just the three starts, putting up her best performance when a close 2nd at Leopardstown over a mile on her second start. Not been seen since the end of September and with this trip likely to be on the short side given her entry in the Irish Oaks although this doesn’t look a particularly strong maiden.
Well-bred Juddmonte filly who is realistically placed on her belated debut. Disappointing if she can't at least make the frame for top connections.
COLLECTING COIN, third on his racecourse debut over 1m at Cork last month, should have come on for that run. Dropped in trip to 7f should suit and could well be able to win this race.
Signs of inexperience on debut over 7f at Gowran on soft ground, doing good work late on having been slowly away. There’s improvement to come and no forlorn hope in this.

Shaped well over fences last time, paying for a big move into contention when fading late on. That was a handicap. Drops down into a beginners chase here, which is there for the taking as she has plenty of experience over the bigger obstacles.

Coffeys Forge won a point a year ago at the 7th attempt after being placed in his previous three points. He joined Gordon Elliott in January and ran reasonably well in three handicap hurdles. Switching to fences for this beginners' chase should give him a chance of his first win under rules.

Not a strong race, and perhaps John O'Connell can get the best from Darkened, who he now trains as well as owns. The selection has some decent form in the book from his time with Noel Kelly, but there is just a suspicion he may be capable of better even at 9 years of age.

Chiefs Kingdom has been placed several times over hurdles and last year switched to fences for two beginners chases in which he ran reasonably well in 4th and 5th. He ran 2nd in a maiden point in March only losing by three quarters of a length after leading and should have a good chance in this maiden hunters chase.

The model I run suggests Squire Ohara should win this one. Squire Ohara has the highest RPR of the runners here. All horses go out carrying the same initial weight. Claiming jockey on board claims 7 lbs, similar to a lot of the other runners, but importantly not at a disadvantage. Great form figures of 2321-2 and should go close again here today.

Ran well on debut last time in what will probably turn out to be a decent race. The winner is already thought good enough to be running in GP Company. Because the selection was a relatively cheap purchase, the terms of this race are in her favor as she receives plenty of weight. Something to bet on here.

Has had a couple of runs, the one at this track far better than his effort at Tipperary. But that experience should prove useful, and the extra furlong here is likely to suit. Worth a small each-way investment in a wide-open race.
Decent debut here over 5f and did not look @ home on Aw @ Dundalk on follow up run. Was only 4/1 & 9/1 for those races so dangerous to let them go off here @ current 40/1 in similar level maidens.

Not a strong event, and despite the lack of a recent run, Gavin Cromwell's new recruit, Arcland, should be good enough to make a winning start for his new trainer with conditions to suit and off a distinctly plausible mark.

Roaring Potter has been off for 1076 days with a back problem, wind op and contractual issues. Everything is tickety-boo now, and he is as fit as they can get him without racing. Trainer Keith Watson has found a good race for his comeback run. The track, trip, ground, and handicap mark all tick the boxes. The two question marks are: has he retained the ability he had, as some horses he has raced against are rated 130+? The other one is his attitude. He can be a bit stubborn sometimes, so Keith left a shotgun at his stable door last night just as an incentive :)

The model I run suggests the value bet here is Wrecking Ball Paul. This result has been driven by Wrecking Ball Paul having the highest RPR of this 10-runner race. He is not really penalized for it in the weights thanks to a kind official ranking. Looks to take advantage of this here and get over the line first in this 2m2f round trip. The model has indicated a 'low' reading here, which translates to a 0.75pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

Looks well treated to my eye. Was running her best race at Thurles the time before last, right there competing until making an error at the hurdle and unable to recover. Dropped a pound for that and then tried in a tongue tie, which did no good. So now, with that removed and a much more experienced jockey in the plate, Me Philip Enright, off bottom weight, she can go close at huge odds.

Highly promising Dark Angel gelding who was rapidly improving throughout last season as a 3yo ending his 3yo campaign with a hat trick of wins defying a penalty in process of completing that hat trick was last seen at Naas 26 days ago where finishing a promising well clear of rest 2nd/7 that was his seasonal reappearance run after a 198 day break and is entitled to strip fitter and be lot sharper at the finish this time out and looks set for another good season steps back up in trip to the 6 furlong trip and G M Lyons's inmate will highly appreciate this extra furlong jockey C T Keane takes the ride that being a positive booking and he has steered My Mate Alfie on those hat hat trick of wins and knows this Dark Angel gelding very well merits serious consideration and shouldn't have a big part to play in this Weatherbys Ireland Greenlands Group 2 Stakes over on the business end

The Irish 2000 Guineas looks to be between the two Juddmonte-owned, English-trained horses. It could go to the less exposed, unbeaten Cosmic Year, especially as Field Of Gold is drawn on the outside and may have to fight his way from the rear of the field again. He may have trouble in running at the Curragh.

Jessie Harrington's charge is the sole Group 1 winner in the field, last year's Futurity Stakes at Doncaster, and as such must look good each way value against the favourite. Indeed, on a line through Wimbledon Hawkeye, he has the beating of the Gosden runner. Described by his trainer as 'feisty' and 'loving a battle,' I think whatever beats him will know he's been in a race.

No doubt Field Of Gold should have won the Guineas when asked for his effort far too late, and he might copy Rosalion in making amends here. But I do think that Officer looks a really good prospect. With FOG having disappointed on his only visit overseas (soft ground also a potential excuse), I'm siding with the O'Brien colt. Raced just once as a juvenile, winning more cosily than the distance suggests, and was pitched into deep company on his first start this year, finishing 3rd in open company behind a race-fit Big Gossey, who is a solid enough yardstick, and Camille Pisarro, who was a Group 1 winner himself as a juvenile and placed 3rd in the French Guineas last time. That on just Officer's 2nd career start was impressive, and he got back to winning ways over C&D in a maiden last time. Hugely unexposed, and I have backed him already for the St James' Palace, where he's a huge 33/1 to take the Paddington route to Royal Ascot success.
